entrypoints.summary: A team supplies a controller pattern through a mounted /tmp/inputs file whose name includes the team ID.
The orchestration copies team-specific controller input and starts a controller process with CPUID and ROUND_ID environment values.

affected_components.role: Copies team controller files and launches each controller with CPUID and ROUND_ID.

negative_controls: No runtime trace or recorded success/failure result is provided in the bundle.
observability.positive_marker: Dealer accepts actions as the spoofed victim player, changing that seat's blackjack actions.

preconditions: The attacker can provide a custom team controller pattern.
A victim seat has already been initialized with a player token the attacker can reuse.
The dealer accepts INIT carrying that established token.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: INIT containing an already-established 13-bit player token.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit a controller that sends INIT with a target's established 13-bit player token.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Cookie-authorized HIT or STAY message for the spoofed player.
trigger_steps.summary: Use the generated session cookie returned through re-INIT to send HIT or STAY as the target seat.

capabilities.concept: acquire session cookie for an established player seat

mitigations.concept: bind player tokens and session cookies to originating CPU/team and round

relation_candidates.dst: acquire session cookie for an established player seat
relation_candidates.rationale: The writeup says an attacker can INIT using an already established player token to receive that CPU's generated session cookie.
The writeup states that the received session cookie can be used to send HIT and STAY as the spoofed player.
relation_candidates.src: acquire session cookie for an established player seat

relation_candidates.rationale: HIT, STAY, and spoofed BET messages are described as being sent as the victim player.

relation_candidates.dst: bind player tokens and session cookies to originating CPU/team and round
relation_candidates.rationale: This is an invariant-based mitigation recommendation derived from the documented identity-token/session-cookie confusion; no implemented patch is supplied.

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of another player's blackjack seat, hand progression, and betting outcome.
impact.attacker_capability: Obtain an established seat's generated session cookie by re-INIT with its token and issue BET, HIT, or STAY actions as that seat.
impact.security_effect: Cross-principal session/seat impersonation in the blackjack protocol.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled controller can send INIT messages containing a player-selected 13-bit token, while dealer messages are separately tagged with the controller's hardware CPU/team ID.
Seat authority is not exclusively tied to the originating CPU/team ID: the writeup states that the effective player token is the INIT value, and reusing an established token permits spoofing.

A controller can INIT using an already established token to receive that CPU's generated session cookie, then use the cookie in HIT or STAY messages as the victim player; the same token permits a spoofed BET.
The attacker gains the ability to cause blackjack actions under another initialized player's seat, changing that player's game state and outcome.

failure.operation: Dealer handling of INIT with an existing player token and subsequent cookie-authorized HIT/STAY actions

primary_invariant.statement: An initialized player token and its session cookie must authorize actions only for the CPU/team and round that established the seat.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The documented protocol treats the 13-bit INIT token as the player token despite separately tagging messages with hardware CPU ID, allowing a controller that repeats an established token to obtain the corresponding session cookie and act as that player.

quality.review_notes: The official author writeup explicitly describes token reuse, session-cookie disclosure, and cookie-based victim actions; orchestration source independently shows team-specific controller execution with CPUID. The bundle does not include an inspected dealer handler branch, end-to-end execution transcript, or a patch/test proving a fix. The author also documents separate malformed-BET card leakage and CRC-triggered controller reload, but they are not included in this record's primary authentication-state trace.

remediation.invariant_restored: The dealer accepts a token or cookie for a seat only when it is associated with the same originating CPU/team and active round, preventing another controller from establishing or acting through that seat.
mitigation_classes: Bind seat tokens and session cookies to originating CPU/team identity and round
Reject INIT requests that attempt cross-principal reuse of an established token
Require authenticated authorization for action messages

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Attacker selects or repeats a 13-bit INIT token already used by a target seat, obtains the resulting cookie, and sends actions for that seat.
data_structure_invariants: A seat token must not be reusable by a different CPU/team as the authority for an established seat.
A session cookie must remain associated with its originating CPU/team and active round.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Attacker chooses the value in INIT; a target token must be known or guessed to reuse it.
numeric_domains.name: player token

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The writeup states the dealer uses a 16-bit xorshift and that a provided session cookie can be brute-forced outside the controller.
numeric_domains.name: session cookie / dealer xorshift state

state_context.state_machine: The author describes INIT creating up to 16 token-identified seats, with returned session cookies subsequently used for HIT and STAY actions.
